documents.title: Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: Item 5a states "Employing AI to complete assignments without explicit permission from the instructor is considered academic dishonesty" and 5d bars AI in quizzes and exams "without express permission", so AI is banned unless the instructor permits it. That is restrict, not delegates, because a default is set.
documents.summary: The LMU Academic Honesty Policy is a general integrity policy with one section on generative AI. It treats unpermitted AI use, unattributed AI content, AI fabrication and AI in assessments as dishonesty, then sets sanctions, procedures and appeals for all violations.

units.why: Item 5a says "Employing AI to complete assignments without explicit permission from the instructor is considered academic dishonesty": AI is banned unless the instructor permits it, so this sets the fallback default (P06) for students; P36 also fits but the permission-default is the distinctive content.
units.anchor: Employing AI to complete assignments without explicit permission from the instructor

units.why: Same sentence classifies unpermitted AI use as "academic dishonesty", i.e. misconduct handled by the integrity process. Coded separately from P06 because it states the classification, not the default.
units.anchor: is considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Employing AI to complete assignments without explicit permission from the instructor is considered academic dishonesty.

units.why: Item 5b says AI content "without proper attribution is considered plagiarism and is strictly forbidden", which demands attribution of AI output; best fits P24 (disclose/cite), since the rule is the attribution duty.
units.anchor: Using AI-generated content without proper attribution is considered plagiarism and is strictly forbidden.

units.why: Item 5b labels unattributed AI content "plagiarism", a misconduct classification under the integrity policy (P36).
units.anchor: considered plagiarism and is strictly forbidden
units.policy: Using AI-generated content without proper attribution is considered plagiarism.

units.why: Item 5c: "Fabricating data or information using AI to deceive is a violation of academic integrity" forbids a specific misuse of AI; closest to P19 (AI may not produce submitted work deceptively).
units.anchor: Fabricating data or information using AI to deceive is a violation of academic integrity.

units.why: Item 5d: "Using AI tools while taking a quiz, an exam, or other in-class or on-line assignment without express permission" is cheating, so AI is barred in assessments unless permitted (P22).
units.anchor: Using AI tools while taking a quiz, an exam, or other in-class

units.why: The opening says "Students are responsible for contacting their instructor(s) before assignments are due" to resolve questions, which tells students to ask when unsure (P10); it applies to AI as part of academic honesty.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for contacting their instructor(s) before assignments are due

units.why: "Students are responsible for understanding the standards of academic honesty" puts accountability on students for knowing the rules, including the AI rules in item 5; P29 (own what you submit) is the nearest accountability type.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding the standards of academic honesty

units.why: Item 3c lists "Using resources and materials prohibited by the Instructor" as cheating, which lets instructors decide which resources (including AI) are banned; this is an instructor-set rule (P04).
units.anchor: Using resources and materials prohibited by the Instructor.

units.why: Item 3d says collaboration "that violates an Instructor's stated policies" is cheating, deferring to instructor-stated rules; the text does not mention AI so it fits P04 only as instructor discretion.
units.anchor: Collaboration on coursework that violates an Instructor's stated policies or instruction.

units.why: Item 1b treats submitting work "obtained via the Internet or a digital source, as one's own work" as plagiarism, the general rule that submitted work must be one's own (P29); it covers AI text by extension but does not name AI.
units.anchor: obtained via the Internet or a digital source, as one's own work

units.why: Item 4c prohibits "distributing any course materials (syllabus, assignments, exams, etc.) without explicit permission from the instructor"; the passage does not name AI, so P49 is only the nearest type.
units.anchor: distributing any course materials (syllabus, assignments, exams, etc.) without explicit permission

units.why: "The burden shall be upon the Instructor to provide evidence that it is more probable than not" sets the evidence standard for any misconduct allegation including AI misuse; fits P64 (fairness in allegations) as a student protection.
units.anchor: The burden shall be upon the Instructor to provide evidence
units.frag_end: committed the alleged academic honesty violation.

units.why: "A Student has the right to appeal the Instructor's decision" gives students a right to respond to allegations (P64).
units.anchor: A Student has the right to appeal the Instructor's decision

units.why: The process section says an instructor "will inform the Student of the suspected academic dishonesty in an email" with evidence and a request to meet, so the student is heard before sanction; best fits P57 (talk with student before escalating).
units.anchor: will inform the Student of the suspected academic dishonesty in an email
units.frag_start: An Instructor who has reason to
units.frag_end: days of discovering evidence of the academic dishonesty.

units.why: The instructor meeting "provides an opportunity for the Instructor and the Student to discuss the suspected academic honesty violation, the evidence", the talk-before-escalating step (P57); distinct from the email notice unit.
units.anchor: an opportunity for the Instructor and the Student to discuss the suspected academic honesty violation
units.frag_end: any concerns the Student may have.

units.why: Sanctions listed include "a requirement to re-do the assignment; a reduced or failing grade", concrete penalties applicable to AI misuse stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: a requirement to re-do the assignment; a reduced or failing grade on an assignment
units.frag_end: a reduced or failing grade in the course.

units.why: Higher sanctions ("Academic probation", "Suspension", "Dismissal") are stated in advance; a separate set of penalties from the instructor-imposed ones (P37).
units.anchor: Suspension from the University.
units.policy: Sanctions for violations include academic probation, suspension and dismissal from the University.

units.why: Escalation by offense: "The presumptive sanction for a second violation is suspension" and third is dismissal, a stated penalty escalation (P37).
units.anchor: The presumptive sanction for a second violation is suspension

units.why: "Factors to be considered in applying sanctions ... shall include the nature and severity of the violation and whether there is a pattern" describes how penalties are scaled; grouped with P37 as penalty rules.
units.anchor: nature and severity of the violation and whether there is a pattern of violations

units.why: "Instructors are expected to apply academic integrity standards consistently ... and pursue all cases of academic dishonesty" binds instructors to enforce, the opposite of declining to police (P60); no type covers a mandatory enforcement duty, so it is UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Instructors are expected to apply academic integrity standards consistently
units.uncovered_note: Instructors must enforce integrity standards consistently and pursue all cases of dishonesty (mandatory enforcement duty).

units.why: "The Provost's office will provide an annual report ... detailing the number and type of violations" is a review/evidence mechanism on integrity cases, fitting P55 (gather evidence), though AI is not named.
units.anchor: annual report, without identifying Students, detailing the number and type of violations
units.frag_end: different areas of the LMU community

units.why: "Records will have a protected status, with access only as authorized" protects confidentiality of integrity case files (privacy); P50 (protect personal data) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Records will have a protected status, with access only as authorized

units.why: The statement of policy says "Violations of academic honesty undermine the fundamental educational mission" and "cannot be tolerated", giving the rationale and institution-level framework behind the AI provisions (P56).
units.anchor: Violations of academic honesty undermine the fundamental educational mission of the University

units.why: The definition of academic honesty, "acknowledge sources consistently and completely", sets the attribution principle behind the AI attribution rule; P24 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: acknowledge sources consistently and completely

units.why: The definitions state "Instructor: any LMU faculty member, librarian, or other individual authorized to evaluate students' academic work", defining who may grant AI permission; P61 (definitions and scope).
units.anchor: any LMU faculty member, librarian, or other individual authorized to evaluate students' academic work

notes: Only the bulletin integrity policy was coded; most units are general integrity rules that govern AI by extension and do not name AI. One UNCOVERED unit: mandatory instructor enforcement.
